rv.q: This feel-good biographical musical brings joy to the stage with a varied score and a star-power performance from Betsy Wolfe.

“Joy: A New True Musical” lies somewhere between the movie and book in tone, but it has a quirkiness all its own, in part because, well, it’s fifteen musical numbers about a woman who sold a mop, but mostly because it exists in an art form that tends to skewer business people.
The show is cute, but overstuffed and wears thin.
Despite a terrific performance by Betsy Wolfe in the title role, the awkwardly titled Joy: A New True Musical needs some serious mopping up.
Joy is a modern fable about resilience and reinvention—with enough heart that sings forth a classically timeless message.
Joy is more than joyful; it is about life filled with possibilities and perseverance.
But once Joy hits her stride, Act II falls apart like an unraveling mop head.
It is entertaining but lacks the elements of good musical theater.

cn.t: Critics find this rags-to-riches musical about inventor Joy Mangano moderately entertaining but uneven, with a weak second act undermining its momentum. Betsy Wolfe's lead performance earns consistent praise across reviews.

vr.q: if you wanna see a musical about strong women chasing their dreams with an incredible cast and fun music then you gotta go see joy
